result.topic_en: The page ends a remark on the mutability of a hemisphere's shape, gives Lexell's rules for approximating the area under a curve from equally spaced ordinates, and gives J. A. Euler's computation of how much the infinite logarithmic curve exceeds its asymptotic axis in length.
result.transcription:

A. m. T. I. p. 10—13.

98.
(Lexell.)
Problema. Ex datis aliquot applicatis aeque distantibus, aream interceptam curvae proxime definire.
(Fig. 62). I. Area $AaBb = AB\left(\frac{Aa+Bb}{2}\right)$
II. » $AaCc = AC\left(\frac{Aa+4Bb+Cc}{6}\right)$
III. » $AaDd = AD\left(\frac{Aa+3Bb+3Cc+Dd}{8}\right)$
IV. » $AaEe = AE\left(\frac{7Aa+32Bb+12Cc+32Dd+7Ee}{90}\right)$
et ita porro. Sit
area $AaXx = AX(\alpha Aa+\beta Bb+\gamma Cc+\delta Dd+\ldots+\xi Xx)$
erit I. $\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta+$ etc. $=1$
II. $\beta+2\gamma+3\delta+4\varepsilon+$ etc. $=\frac{4}{2}=\frac{2^2}{2}$
III. $\beta+2^2\gamma+3^2\delta+4^2\varepsilon+$ etc. $=\frac{2^4}{3}$
IV. $\beta+2^3\gamma+3^3\delta+4^3\varepsilon+$ etc. $=\frac{2^6}{4}$
V. $\beta+2^4\gamma+3^4\delta+4^4\varepsilon+$ etc. $=\frac{2^8}{5}$
et sic porro.
A. m. T. I. p. 128.

99.
(J. A. Euler.)
In logarithmica (Fig. 63), cujus subtangens $AD=1$, ab applicata $AB=1$ longitudo curvae in infinitum extensae $BU$ superat axem $AV$ etiam in infinitum productum quantitate $\sqrt{2}-1-l\frac{\sqrt{2}+1}{2}$. Nam sit abscissa $AP=x$ et $PM=y$, erit $y=e^{-x}$, hinc $dy=-e^{-x}dx$, et elementum arcus $=dx\sqrt{(1+e^{-2x})}$, hinc
$BM-AP=\int dx\left(\sqrt{(1+e^{-2x})}-1\right)$
quod integrale ab $x=0$ usque ad $x=\infty$ extendi debet.
Ponatur $\sqrt{(1+e^{-2x})}-1=z$, fiet $e^{-2x}=2z+zz$ et $-2x=l(2z+zz)$; ubi pro $x=0$ habemus $z=\sqrt{2}-1$, et pro $x=\infty$ fit $z=0$; hinc differentiando
$-dx=\frac{dz(1+z)}{2z+zz}$, et formula nostra fit $-\int\frac{dz(1+z)}{2+z}$
quae integrari debet ab $z=\sqrt{2}-1$ usque ad $z=0$, vel nostra formula erit
$-dz\left(1-\frac{1}{2+z}\right)$, ergo integrando $-z+l(2+z)+\sqrt{2}-1-l(1+\sqrt{2})$.
Nunc fiat $z=0$, et quantitas quaesita erit
$\sqrt{2}-1+l2-l(1+\sqrt{2})=\sqrt{2}-1+l\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}+1}$.
A. m. T. I. p. 258.

items.quote: Interim patet hemisphaerii figuram certe esse mutabilem; cujusmodi autem mutationes recipere possit, problema videtur difficillimum.
items.english: Meanwhile it is clear that the figure of a hemisphere is certainly mutable; but what kind of changes it can undergo seems to be a most difficult problem.

items.quote: In logarithmica (Fig. 63), cujus subtangens $AD=1$, ab applicata $AB=1$ longitudo curvae in infinitum extensae $BU$ superat axem $AV$ etiam in infinitum productum quantitate $\sqrt{2}-1-l\frac{\sqrt{2}+1}{2}$.
items.english: In the logarithmic curve whose subtangent AD = 1, the length of the curve BU, extended to infinity from the ordinate AB = 1, exceeds the axis AV, also produced to infinity, by the quantity √2 − 1 − ln((√2+1)/2).
